text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Two Australian and New Zealand parliamentary delegations arrived in Hanoi on Monday for a five-day visit to examine Vietnam's health care and family planning schemes and policy.

-- Egypt and Vietnam are expecting to sign 18 agreements to promote bilateral co-operation. Egypt's national airline, Egypt Air, is expected to make Hanoi part of its Cairo-Bangkok-Beijing route by the end of this year.
-- Vietnam's commercial banks have been given the green light from the government to honor due letters of credit issued on behalf of Minh Phung and EPCO companies.

-- The Ministry of Communications and Transport and the Japanese International Cooperation Agency are presently preparing projects for developing three deepwater seaports at Dung Quat, Chan May and Lien Cheu in Central Vietnam.

-- Water levels on the northern Red and Thai Binh rivers are rising because of heavy rains. The National Committee for Flood Protection has asked local areas to secure measures to protect river dykes.
-- Vietnam has opened a new war cemetery beside National Route Nine for the remains of nearly 10,000 martyrs sacrificed during the war against the Americans.
-- 99.02 percent of voters in 56 of Vietnam's 61 provinces cast votes in Sunday's elections for the tenth session of the National Assembly, according to latest figures.
-- A three-day trial related to the biggest-ever drugs case in Vietnam, originally scheduled to open on Thursday, has been postponed.
-- Vietnam's Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam is taking part in the 30th Foreign Ministers' ASEAN conference, which starts on Wednesday in Malaysia.
